correctness.rationale: The graph is specified by 24 explicit vertices and the 36 edges of the documented LCF construction. A 23-by-23 reduced integer Laplacian is transformed by 471 listed unimodular row/column operations to the exact divisibility-chain diagonal of nineteen units followed by 11, 44, 132, 2640. The complete operations and replaying checker are included. An independent edge realization and different modular Smith algorithm give 2-primary exponents (2,2,4), 3-primary (1,1), 5-primary (1), 11-primary (1,1,1,1), and a Bareiss determinant of 168664320. Both programs were run on the embedded paths. No claim of infinite-family generality is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general construction of a critical group does not evaluate its finite abelian invariant factors. The McGee graph is 3-regular with girth 7 and is not complete multipartite or vertex-transitive, so the cited complete multipartite and Cayley results do not cover it. A spectral formula can recover the number of spanning trees but not, by itself, the integer Smith factors. The inaccessible spectral-cage paper remains a residual rather than being certified noncovering.

originality.rationale: The new content is the full integer Smith decomposition, not the 1960 cage construction, its known adjacency spectrum, or the publicly indexed count of 168664320 spanning trees. The McGee (1960) four-page primary source and complete MathWorld entry were inspected, and the House of Graphs indexed invariant list already contains the determinant but not invariant factors. Targeted equivalence/alias, exact-value, and broader-class searches, together with the public research-record semantic searches, exposed no covering result. The high-value spectral-cage article could not be inspected in full and remains an explicitly recorded risk; this is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a priority proof.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed graph-sandpile/SNF tables could state the same McGee-specific decomposition.
The relevant 2025 spectral-cage article was not accessible in full; accessible abstract alone cannot justify a whole-paper noncoverage judgment.

value.rationale: The uniquely smallest cubic girth-seven graph is a canonical extremal finite graph with a previously tabulated tree count but no located full sandpile decomposition. The complete integral discriminant group determines its chip-firing equivalence classes, exact exponent, minimal generator number, and prime-by-prime singularity of the reduced Laplacian, including four independent 11-torsion directions; these are not implied by the known tree total or adjacency spectrum. These are natural arithmetic invariants of an extremal graph, suitable for future network/divisor and finite-field harmonic comparisons, not an arbitrary induced-subgraph slice. Narrow single-graph scope and unknown historical priority are acknowledged.
